{"title":"The Dino Team by the Sea","level":2,"topic":"dinosaurs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya and her dino team go to the sea.

Then they see it! A bone in the sand. It is a real dino bone!

Maya cleans the bone. She sees each groove. "This is from a dino that lived long ago," she says.

Some scientists find bones and teach us about dinosaurs. They read the bones like a book!

Maya will keep the bone safe. She will take it home and paint a sign for it.

Oak roars. Rain roars. Maya roars too!","cover_scene":"A girl with a small backpack kneels on a sunny beach beside a long-necked green dinosaur and a small speedy dinosaur, holding up a sandy fossil bone as waves roll in."}

{"title":"Toad and the Big Dino Race Day","level":2,"topic":"obstacle race","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Sixty dinos came to race today. Big ones. Small ones. Fast ones!

transcript.title: The Dino Team by the Sea
transcript.text:
Maya and her dino team go to the sea.

The big one is Oak. Oak has a long neck. He can reach a leaf at the top of a tree.

The small one is Rain. Rain can run on the sand and leap over a boat.

"Let's go on a trail!" says Maya.

The trail goes past the beach. Oak eats green leaves. Rain sniffs the salt air.

Then they see it! A bone in the sand. It is a real dino bone!

Maya cleans the bone. She sees each groove. "This is from a dino that lived long ago," she says.

Some scientists find bones and teach us about dinosaurs. They read the bones like a book!

Maya will keep the bone safe. She will take it home and paint a sign for it.

The sign says: DINO TEAM. GREAT FIND!

Oak roars. Rain roars. Maya roars too!

transcript.title: The Moon Turns Red
transcript.text:
One late night, Maya and Dave went up on the roof.

"Wake up, Dave," said Maya. "The moon will change tonight!"

Dave gave a wide yawn. He sat close to Maya.

The moon was white and round. Then a dark shape slid on it.

Slow. Slow. Slow.

"That is us," said Maya. "That shade is made by Earth! We are in the way of the sun."

Bit by bit, the white moon was gone. In its place was a deep red moon.

Dave hid his face.

"Do not hide," said Maya. "It is safe. It is just red light. It is not a bite from a space beast!"

Dave took a look. He gave a small smile.

They sat side by side and did not speak.

Then Maya said, "That is the best thing I have ever seen."

Dave gave a soft roar. Same, Maya. Same.

chapters.title: Maya and the Bubble Rocket
chapters.text:
Maya wants to make a rocket.

Not a big one. A bubble rocket!

NASA has a plan for kids. You can make a rocket that pops up with bubbles. Maya reads the plan.

She will take a jar. She will shake it. Shake, shake, shake!

The fizz will make gas. The gas will push. Up goes the rocket!

"Take it out to the yard," said Dad.

Maya sets the rocket on the flat rock by the lake.

She drops in the fizz. She gives it one big shake.

Then she runs back.

Pop! The rocket jumps up. It flies past the gate!

"That was not fake!" said Maya. "That was a real launch!"

Dad helps her bake a cake to mark the day. The cake has a red rocket on top.

Maya takes a big bite.

"Same time next week," she said. "I will make it go up to the moon!"

transcript.title: The Puff Planet
transcript.text:
Maya read the space news. "Wow, Dave! Look at this."

Some planets are puffy. They are huge, but they weigh next to nothing. They are less dense than cotton candy!

"Let's go see one," said Maya.

They rode the rocket a long, long time. Then a pale pink ball came into sight.

"That is the place!" said Maya.

Dave took a big step onto it. He did not land hard. He sank in slow, like a foot in a cake.

Maya gave a laugh. She made a jump. She rose way up high, then came down like a leaf.

Dave rolled. Maya slid. They made a puff planet slide!

Then Maya took a bite of the pink fluff. "It is not candy," she said. "It is just gas."

Dave gave a wave at Earth, the blue dot far away.

Time to ride home.

chapters.title: Nine, Eight, Ride!

Maya has a red rocket.

She will take a ride.

Nine. Eight. Go!

Stars hide in the black.

Maya sits by the side of Pip the dog.

"Can we ride to the moon?" Maya said.

Pip barks. Yes!

The moon is a big white rock.

Maya steps out. She can glide!

Pip can glide too. Hop, hop, hop!

They slide down a moon hill.

Maya digs. She finds a moon stone.

It is smooth and wide.

"I will take it home," she said.

Back in the rocket, nine, eight, go!

Down, down to her yard.

Mom and Dad wave.

They ride bikes to school.

Maya has the moon stone in her hand.

Her class makes news. Kids read it!

"Maya had a moon ride," said the page.

Maya smiles a wide smile.

Nine. Eight. Read!

transcript.title: Dave and the Space Rock
transcript.text:
A space rock fell in Maya's yard at nine.

It made a hole the size of a bike.

Dave came to look. He gave the rock a sniff.

"Do not bite it!" said Maya.

The rock was not hot. It was smooth like glass. It had lines of white in it.

Maya put it in her case and rode her bike to the space lab.

A man at the lab took a close look.

"This came from far, far away," he said. "It is very old. Older than dinos!"

Dave gave a proud roar.

"Can we keep it?" said Maya.

"You can. But let us take five small bits for tests."

So Maya came home with her space rock. She made a fine base for it out of a plate.

Dave slept by it all night.

Same time, same rock, same best pals.

transcript.title: The Nine Mile Space Kite
transcript.text:
Maya had a wild plan. She wanted to fly a kite in space.

"A kite needs wind," said Dave, "and space has none."

"Then we will make our own," said Maya with a smile.

She made a kite of thin white tape, wide as a gate. Sunlight would push it, just like wind pushes a sail. Real space teams use sails like this!

They rode the rocket up nine miles, then nine more. Maya let the kite slide out of the side hatch.

The sun hit the pale tape. The kite rose! It did not shake or dive. It just glided, slow and fine.

Dave held the line with his huge nose. Maya took notes in her case-bound book.

They flew the kite past the white moon and came home late.

"Same time next week?" said Maya.

Dave gave one proud, huge nod.

Rex flies back down. Dino books say dinos can not fly.

But this dino did! Rex flew in a rocket, one time, all the way up.

Made. Tape. Time. Home. Good job!

transcript.title: The Lost Space Probe
transcript.text:
Far past the red planet, a tiny probe had gone quiet. Nobody on Earth could trace it.

"We will find it," said Maya. Dave gave a huge nod.

They rode for nine days. Dave slept the whole time and woke up just once, to eat a crate of grapes.

Then Maya spotted a pale shape spinning in the dark. It was the probe! Its side was dented, and its wide dish was tipped the wrong way.

Maya slid out on a safety line. She took a wrench from her case and gave the dish a careful shove. It slid back into place.

A green light woke up on the probe. Then a beep. Then five more beeps.

"It is alive!" Maya cried.

Back home, scientists smiled at their screens. New pictures of far stars came flowing in.

Dave just yawned. Then he ate five more grapes.

chapters.title: The Dino Bone Hunt
chapters.text:
Sam digs in the sun. He has a big hat and a tape.

Dig, dig, dig. Sam sees a bone!

It is a huge bone. It is as wide as a gate.

"Can I take it home?" Sam asks.

"Yes," says Mom. "Put it in a safe case."

Sam finds more. He finds a spike. He finds a bone the size of a cake pan.

A dino bit a pine cone here, long ago! It had a long spine and a fine tail.

Sam makes a note. He writes the name of each bone. He writes the date.

Then Sam and Mom ride home.

Sam can see dino facts on a tape and in a game. Dino fans make maps. Dino fans dig and hope.

Sam has a plan. "Next time," he says, "I will find a whole dino!"

He smiles a wide smile.

transcript.title: The Ice Lake on Mars
transcript.text:
Maya and Dave rode the rocket to Mars. The whole place was red, like rust.

"Space teams think there is ice here," said Maya. "Frozen lakes, hid under the stone."

They drove a rover for nine miles. Dave took the wheel once. They spun in a wide circle and had to stop.

Then Maya saw a shine. In a deep hole was a plate of pale blue ice, smooth as glass.

"A lake!" she cried. "A real one!"

She chipped off a small cube and slid it into her case. Dave wanted to take a bite. Maya shook her head.

"Not this time," she said with a smile. "This cube is for the lab."

Ice means water. Water means people could live here, one fine day.

They rode home late, nine days of space and stars.

Dave slept the whole ride. He dreamed of grapes.

chapters.title: The Bubble Rocket Ride
chapters.text:
Maya and Sam made a bubble rocket.

They used a tube. They taped the top. Pop! Up it rose.

"That rocket rose nine feet!" said Sam.

NASA kids make bubble rockets too. You can make one at home.

Maya made hers slim like a cone. Sam made his wide.

Maya had a plan. She wrote a name on the side. The name was Space Mule.

"Time to race," said Sam.

Three, two, one! Both rockets rose. Space Mule rose high. It came down on the same spot. Sam's rocket rose, then fell in the lake.

"Oh no! It is not safe!" said Sam.

But Maya had a rope. She got it back. It was fine. Just wet.

"Let us make five more," said Maya. "One for each rock in space. Mars. Mercury. Nine rockets in all!"

Sam gave a wave. "Time to fly home," he said.

transcript.title: Mars Is a Wild Place
transcript.text:
Maya and Dave go to Mars.

Mars is a place.

p - l - a - c - e. Place!

Mars is red. Mars has ice at the top and the base.

Mars has a big hole in the ground. It is nine miles deep!

Maya can not take off her space hat.

The air on Mars is thin. You can not take a breath of it.

"Keep it on, Dave," says Maya. "That is the rule."

Dave keeps his on.

They ride up a slope. It is a huge old flame hill. It blew hot rock long ago.

Maya makes a note. She puts it in her case.

The sun goes down. The sky is pale pink.

"What a fine day," says Maya.

Dave gives a smile.

Time to ride home.

Same trip next week!

chapters.title: The Planet with No Sun
chapters.text:
Sky Club met at nine.

"I have news," said Mom. "Star experts found a planet with no sun!"

Maya sat up. "No sun? Is it home to anyone?"

"It is not," said Mom. "It is cold as stone."

Maya drew it. She drew a big dome. She drew nine white dots.

"Can I name it?" Maya said.

"Name it," said Mom.

Maya wrote: LONE PLANET. She made the line thin. She made the dome wide.

"It has no sun," Maya said. "But it is not sad. It can glide. It can ride in the dark. It is not tame!"

Mom gave Maya a smile. "That is a fine tale."

Maya put her page on the wall at home.

Lone. Stone. Home. Alone.

But not sad.

The lone planet can hide in space, Maya said. And I can find it.
